items.title: E1.11 Data conventions
items.body:
As a customer, I want one installation per company with strict per-site separation so my warehouses' data never mixes and my supervisors see only their sites.

### Acceptance criteria

- Single-tenant per install (one company per database; no tenant_id). A hosted offering would be siloed: one database and one Kubernetes namespace per customer.
- Unit of work = one DbContext per request/job (behind `IUnitOfWork`); single `SaveChanges` per operation; explicit transactions only for listed multi-step operations (deposit replay, marriage, intake, settings cascade, lease release/expiry) and kept free of non-database I/O; no distributed transactions (outbox carries side effects); read-committed isolation.
- Data access: repository per aggregate (not per table) — a specific interface per aggregate (`ISkuRepository`, `IZoneGroupRepository`, `IReleaseRepository`, …) inheriting the generic base interfaces `IReadOnlyRepository<T,TId>`, `ISearchableRepository<T>`, `IWriteOnlyRepository<T>` (candidate for a `Wolfgang.Repositories` library) and adding the few business-named methods that need EF (`GetForUpdateAsync`, `GetByBarcodeAsync`, `GetChangedSinceAsync`); master-data CRUD comes from the base for free. Repositories fetch and persist aggregates; handlers own orchestration and rules; cross-aggregate work is a handler using several repositories inside one `IUnitOfWork`.
- `IUnitOfWork` is a thin seam over `DbContext` — `SaveChangesAsync` and `ExecuteInTransactionAsync(Func<…>)` only (delegate form so rollback and EF retry are automatic); no `Set<T>()`, no change-tracker access. Handlers reference repositories and `IUnitOfWork`, never `DbContext` (architecture test); repository interfaces never expose `IQueryable`, `DbContext`, or expression-tree search (criteria objects only, AOT-safe).
- Reads for screens and reports stay separate: query classes projecting to records, not repositories — the place where Dapper is benchmarked (E36.5). Handler unit tests use fakes of the repository interfaces; DbContextBuilder tests the EF repositories themselves.
- `site_id` on all site-scoped entities with an EF global query filter from the caller's site context; cross-site reads require `IgnoreQueryFilters()` behind a permission; writes outside scope rejected at `SaveChanges`; global tables (users, roles, global settings, SKUs, barcodes, license) unfiltered; `site_id` leads most indexes.

items.title: [Phase 17] Keep body-free communication history with one expiring support-safe sent copy
items.body:
<!-- phase17-publisher:892021160128fcb0ecd5fc8f:T23 -->

## Parent

#873 — the Phase 17 System Messages & Template Management epic.

## Why this exists (domain context)

Staff need to answer practical questions such as “which message contract ran, for whom, through which sender, and what did the provider report?” They sometimes also need to see the recently sent wording to support a donor. Persisting every personalized subject and body indefinitely would turn the communication ledger into a searchable archive of donor PII, protected links, financial facts, security content, and restricted ministry information. Resend's provider history is temporary external custody and cannot become Asym's product truth. Official receipts, statements, and source records remain owned by their producing phases.

Phase 6 #550 is the one durable communication spine. This slice evolves it into useful body-free history and adds one deliberately subordinate tenant-only **Recent sent copy**. The durable event remains readable after content expiry through stable contract/source/publication/provider evidence. An eligible support-safe copy exists only for 0, 7, or 30 days, is separately encrypted and authorized, cannot be searched/exported or used to retry, and disappears immediately from authorization at expiry or privacy revocation. Platform-scoped communication never receives a readable copy in this generation.

The UX must be honest and easy: history shows what is known without implying delivery or reading; an authorized staff member uses one secondary **View sent copy** action; the viewer explains exactly why content is available or unavailable and always points to the durable source/artifact where permitted. This slice implements D14 and ADR-0031 without building a legal archive, provider-message browser, or support inbox.

## What to build

1. Evolve the Phase 6 communication-history projection so every event records the exact `ExecutionScope`, contract key/version/generation, source reference/fence, plan/step, purpose/classification, requested/effective locale, resolution-trace hash, publication/dependency hashes, permanent semantic/member identity, timestamps, safe title/classification, integrity hashes, correction/supersession links, and content-free audit evidence.
2. Keep channel-specific evidence structurally separate. External-delivery events may reference nonsecret sender/reply/delivery-profile snapshots, preparation/provider identities, and normalized outcomes. `in_product` events retain local `available` and presentation truth and cannot carry preparation, provider identity/state/outcome, sender, or connection fields.
3. Prohibit durable personalized body, ordinary personalized subject, protected URL/action, credentials, attachment/artifact bytes, arbitrary provider payload, raw headers/errors, full click URL, IP, user agent, recipient secret, care/restricted facts, and official document bytes. Add database/service/DTO/log tests that enforce this negative contract.
4. Add one tenant setting with exactly **30 days — Recommended**, **7 days**, or **Do not store readable copies**. Combine it with the contract's closed class: `ordinary_support_copy` (maximum 30 days), `limited_support_copy` (maximum 7 days), or `no_readable_copy` (zero). Effective retention is the shorter bound; unknown/invalid class is zero. Shortening applies immediately after a count-only impact confirmation; lengthening affects only future captures.
5. At T15's prepared/provider-crossing boundary, create at most one separately encrypted, recipient-specific support projection for an eligible tenant email. Allow only support-safe resolved subject/preheader, sanitized inert HTML and complete plain text, safe sender/reply labels, effective locale, and nonsecret catalog title. Strip every URL/action target, token/code, attachment/artifact body, tracking element/query, remote asset, raw header/provider field, internal id, care/restricted value, and contract-forbidden fact. The copy must never reconstruct provider bytes.
6. Freeze `expires_at` from the first durable instant provider submission may have occurred. Future-scheduled work starts the clock at provider crossing, not queue time. Viewing, retry, delivery delay, bounce/complaint, reconciliation, provider events, or staff activity never extends it. Pre-provider definite no-send retains no convenience copy; possible submission may retain the one prepared copy until the unchanged expiry.
7. Implement an idempotent, scope-owner-fair purge worker. Authorization denies at the exact expiry/restriction instant; primary ciphertext and key material purge within the documented operational window, leaving only content-free tombstone/evidence. Reclassification, privacy incident, Party/contact authority loss, tenant offboarding, erasure, and policy shortening may priority-deny and purge without deleting body-free history or official artifacts.
8. Build body-free history list/detail queries with keyset pagination and current capability/site/Party projection. Add a deliberate Recent-copy reveal command requiring `system_messages.recent_copy.reveal` plus current tenant, role/capability, exact recipient Party/contact revision, source/site, privacy class, restriction/erasure, and unexpired-copy authority. Source/fund access alone is insufficient. Record content-free allow/deny audit.
9. Deliver an inert viewer: private/no-store response, no prefetch or prerender, restrictive CSP, sandbox without scripts/forms/navigation/popups/downloads/external resources, no analytics/third-party receiver, complete plain text, and client-state clearing on close, expiry, tenant/role change, or authorization loss.
10. Render the complete truthful states: **Sent copy** only with provider-acceptance evidence; **Attempted copy** for provider-bound failed/indeterminate work; **Not sent** for definite pre-provider stop; expired date; organization-disabled; security-class denied; privacy-removed; official-wrapper expired; capture unavailable; temporarily unavailable; insufficient permission; and honest legacy-without-copy. A sample design preview is synthetic and labeled, never reconstructed history.
11. Reconcile existing `email_send_logs`, `email_events`, receipt and contribution-notification references into body-free aliases or migration adapters. Do not rewrite history to claim absent scope, recipient, provider, review, or retention proof. T32 owns the final reader/writer cutover and legacy contraction.
12. Document external custody plainly: the tenant's Asym 0/7/30 choice controls only the Asym support copy and does not shorten or delete data in the tenant's Resend account. Re-verify current Resend retention documentation at build time rather than embedding a timeless promise.

## Data model (this slice)

T15 owns the core `communication_intents`, `communication_preparations`, and external prepared artifacts. T21 owns normalized provider evidence. This slice evolves `communication_events` and creates `communication_recent_sent_copies` without a second ledger:

- `communication_events` — append-only body-free facts with the complete `ExecutionScope` owner arc, same-scope intent/result references, immutable contract/source/publication/locale/member identity, channel-discriminated evidence, correction/supersession, safe title, hashes, timestamps, and audit. Database checks prohibit provider fields for `in_product` and prohibit tenant/Party fields for platform scope.
- `communication_recent_sent_copies` — **tenant-only** row keyed to one same-tenant preparation and exact Party/contact-point revision; closed copy class/policy version; separately encrypted allow-listed subject/preheader/HTML/text and safe display labels; purpose-separated AAD binding tenant, environment, preparation, copy row, recipient/contact revision, policy revision, and key revision; `captured_at`, immutable `expires_at`, access-denied/purge/backup/erasure facts, and content-free tombstone.
- a small tenant recent-copy policy head/version on the existing tenant email/settings aggregate or an equivalent nonduplicative settings record, with choice, expected revision, actor, impact count/hash, effective time, and audit.

Every tenant relationship uses `tenant_id NOT NULL` and composite same-tenant FKs. Recent copies require FORCE RLS or stricter service-only access plus an explicit server reveal path; tenant/client roles never select ciphertext. Platform `scope_kind` is structurally prohibited from recent-copy rows. Append-only history cannot cascade-delete when copy material is purged. Index history by scope owner plus keyset cursor/state/time, and purge by tenant plus expiry cursor; measure before partitioning.

The encrypted copy is not deduplicated across tenants or recipients. A digest may support integrity but may not become cross-tenant equality evidence, search, cache key, or authorization. Backups must replay expiry/erasure/restriction/offboarding ledgers before any decrypt path is enabled.

## Module interface

Expose body-free queries and one narrow reveal command:

```ts
type RecentCopyPolicy = "thirty_days" | "seven_days" | "off";
type RecentCopyClass =
  | "ordinary_support_copy"
  | "limited_support_copy"
  | "no_readable_copy";

type CommunicationHistoryDetail = {
  eventId: string;
  safeTitle: string;
  channel: "email" | "in_product";
  contract: { key: string; version: number; generation: number };
  source: SafeSourceReference;
  locale: { requested: string; effective: string; traceHash: string };
  outcome: BodyFreeOutcomeProjection;
  recentCopy: RecentCopyAvailability;
  correctionLinks: readonly SafeHistoryLink[];
};

listCommunicationHistory(query: AuthorizedHistoryQuery): Promise<CursorPage<CommunicationHistorySummary>>;
readCommunicationHistory(query: AuthorizedHistoryDetailQuery): Promise<CommunicationHistoryDetail>;
revealRecentSentCopy(command: {
  eventId: string;
  expectedCopyRevision: number;
  currentRecipientAuthority: RecipientAuthorityProof;
}): Promise<RecentCopyRevealResult>;
purgeExpiredRecentCopies(command: BoundedPurgeClaim): Promise<PurgeBatchResult>;
```

`RecentCopyRevealResult` is a closed union for available, expired, disabled, denied-class, privacy-removed, capture-unavailable, temporary-unavailable, not-authorized, and legacy-unknown. It returns inert support content only for `available`; every branch returns safe explanation and durable evidence/source next action. The caller never supplies tenant/scope, recipient, class, expiry, or ciphertext key. Do not add a generic content blob service, arbitrary history metadata bag, provider-fetch fallback, or body-search endpoint.

## Repo anchors (REAL vs FORWARD)

- **REAL — current history tables:** `supabase/schema.sql` defines `email_send_logs` and `email_events`, including personalized/provider-era fields and service-role access. They are migration evidence, not the final Phase 6 event authority.
- **REAL — current event reducer:** `packages/api/src/email/webhooks/resend.ts` inserts `email_events` and updates send-log status. T21 replaces payload/address-based owner inference with signed matching-connection evidence; this slice consumes its normalized body-free result.
- **REAL — receipt writer:** `packages/api/src/giving/receipts.ts` writes `email_send_logs` after a direct send. Its idempotency and `receipt_send_log_id` relationships must be mapped before T32 removes the old authority.
- **REAL — contribution-notification history:** `packages/api/src/admin/contribution-operations/notifications/store.ts` persists provider message ids and history inputs; contribution-operation approval/correction paths are census/migration consumers, not a parallel ledger.
- **REAL — template evidence:** `packages/api/src/email/template-store.ts` stores source/version/compiled output and can support a synthetic pinned-design preview. Template rows cannot reconstruct a personalized historical send.
- **REAL — authorization/audit conventions:** `packages/api/src/shared/with-operation.ts` and `packages/lib/audit/logger.ts` provide authenticated operation and audit precedents; reveal needs a stricter content-specific current-authority check.
- **REAL — normative contracts:** Phase 6 PRD `docs/prds/sitestacker-parity/phase-06-shared-communication-event-model.md`, Phase 10 epic #628, Phase 12 epic #665, ADR-0031, and the Phase 17 OpenSpec history requirement bind ownership and privacy.
- **FORWARD — Phase 6/17 history modules:** `packages/api/src/communications/history.*`, `recent-copy.*`, tenant recent-copy policy, body-free event evolution, reveal viewer, and purge worker do not exist yet.
- **FORWARD — unified History UX:** T29 will compose these working list/detail/reveal surfaces into the System Messages workspace. T32 owns final compatibility-reader contraction.

## Congruence constraints (binding)

- Implement D14 and ADR-0031. Phase 6 #550 is the sole recipient-specific intent/provider/history writer; this slice may evolve it but must not create a second history ledger.
- Phase 7 #566, Phase 8 #587, Phase 18, and Phase 19 remain owners of official receipt/statement/document truth and bytes. A recent email wrapper is not the artifact.
- Durable history is body-free for tenant and platform branches. Platform rows are service-only and force `no_readable_copy`; tenant settings/capabilities cannot grant platform-copy access.
- Provider acceptance, mail-server delivery, reading, understanding, payment, receipt finality, and business completion are distinct. History labels must not collapse them.
- Recent copy is a convenience projection only. It cannot dispatch, retry, reconstruct provider bytes, satisfy legal retention, feed search/export, populate AI context, or authorize an action.
- Copy access requires both source/site and exact recipient Party/contact authority. Phase 10 restriction/erasure and Phase 12 current capabilities override a stale page/session.
- Expiry is nonextendable per copy. A policy increase, view, retry, webhook, delayed delivery, provider reconciliation, restore, or staff edit never resurrects or extends content.
- Provider retention is external custody. Do not fetch bodies from Resend, claim provider deletion, or present provider history as Asym communication truth.

**Do not over-engineer.** Build one body-free event projection, one three-choice tenant policy, one finite copy-class map, one separately encrypted recent copy, one reveal path/viewer, one purge worker, and focused history queries. Do not build body search, legal hold, indefinite archive, data warehouse, provider inbox mirror, e-discovery, generalized encrypted blob storage, or a second audit system.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Durable history contains the complete safe contract/source/member/locale/publication/provider evidence needed to explain a send while schema, DTO, log, and fixture tests prove it stores no personalized body/ordinary subject, URL/token, credential, raw provider material, IP/user agent, care/restricted fact, or official document bytes.
- [ ] Tenant and platform event rows satisfy the exclusive scope/recipient/profile arcs; every tenant/client role is denied platform history, and an `in_product` event cannot acquire provider fields.
- [ ] The 30/7/Off policy combines with the closed contract maximum using the shorter bound; unknown class is zero, shortening is immediate after count-only confirmation, and lengthening affects future copies only.
- [ ] At most one eligible copy is sealed at provider crossing with the exact allow-listed support projection and purpose-separated encryption context; pre-provider no-send creates none.
- [ ] Platform scope and denied classes cannot insert, query, decrypt, or reveal a recent-copy row.
- [ ] Reveal re-proves current tenant, capability, exact Party/contact revision, source/site, privacy/restriction/erasure, and expiry; source access without recipient authority is denied before decryption and records a content-free denial audit.
- [ ] The viewer is private/no-store, sandboxed, no-network/no-script/no-form/no-navigation/no-download/no-analytics, plain-text complete, keyboard/screen-reader usable, and clears client content on close or authority loss.
- [ ] Authorization stops exactly at expiry/restriction time even if purge is delayed; purge is idempotent, observable, fair, and leaves history/official artifacts intact. Backup restore cannot resurrect readable expired or erased content.
- [ ] History distinguishes Sent/Attempted/Not sent and every specified unavailable-copy state without claiming Delivered, Read, Received, Paid, or Completed beyond owning evidence.
- [ ] Legacy logs/events are classified honestly and linked prospectively; absent scope, recipient, provider, consent, review, or copy evidence stays unknown rather than being fabricated.
- [ ] The UI and docs state that Asym retention does not control the tenant's Resend retention and link to build-time-verified provider guidance.

## Testing

- Migration/RLS tests cover exclusive tenant/platform arcs, composite same-tenant FKs, append-only history, provider-field prohibition on `in_product`, platform-copy insertion denial, reveal service isolation, expiry indexes, and purge-without-cascade.
- Unit-test copy eligibility for every class × tenant policy × shorter contract/source/privacy bound, unknown class, future schedule, pre-provider stop, possible submission, policy shortening/lengthening, and exact expiry instant.
- Use hostile projection fixtures containing action URLs, codes/tokens, attachments, payment/staff/care/restricted facts, remote images, tracking queries, internal ids, raw headers/errors, and provider fields; assert none survive storage, viewer DTO, logs, metrics, traces, audit, export, or cache.
- Authorization-test valid reveal, source-only access, changed tenant, revoked role/capability, Party merge/relink, changed contact revision, site loss, Phase 10 reclassification, erasure, expiry, offboarding, stale tab, impersonation, platform scope, and guessed ids.
- Browser/security-test CSP and sandbox, blocked network, scripts/forms/navigation/popups/downloads, prefetch/prerender, analytics, client cache, copy-state clearing, XSS/bidi content, and plain-text fallback.
- Race-test capture/submit/cancel, expiry/read, purge/read, restriction/read, policy-change/capture, backup restore, duplicate purge, and batch recipients with different deadlines. Privacy denial wins readability without rewriting provider outcome.
- Test history pagination and projections at high row counts without N+1 provider/source reads; verify cross-tenant cache/cursor isolation and low-cardinality telemetry.
- Add component/E2E coverage for loading, empty, body-free detail, available copy, every unavailable state, permission loss, network failure, keyboard/focus, screen reader, mobile/reflow, long locale, RTL/bidi, and honest provider/business wording.
- Update retention, support reveal, privacy purge, restore, offboarding, and rollback runbooks. Include an overdue-purge alert fixture consumed by T31.

## Blocked by

- #888 — the single Phase 6 plan/intent/preparation/dispatch boundary that owns the communication occurrence.
- #894 — signed matching-owner provider-event evidence and normalized provider identity.

External contracts consumed at implementation: Phase 6 epic #550, Phase 10 epic #628, and Phase 12 epic #665. This ticket does not dispatch any message.

items.title: [SPEC] §4.2 Full 35-Schema DDL (Schemas 13-35): Remaining schema DDL for credit, coaching, pathway, billing, notification, partner, application, event-log, audit-log, vector-embeddings, BAI, marketplace, lender, EDO, and telemetry schemas
items.body:
---
owner: service:platform
depends_on: ["1625"]
blocks: []
spec_sections: ["§4.2"]
blueprint_sections: ["§17", "§33"]
maturity_target: Foundation
acceptance:
  - DDL committed for schemas 13-35 covering: credit (personal and business bureau data, tradeline inventory, CLI tracking), coaching (session logs, prompt registry, coaching milestones), pathway (capital plan, product eligibility, submission history), billing (subscription tiers, invoice history, referral fee ledger), notification (email/SMS event log), partner (lender partner profiles, cohort subscriptions), application (loan application submissions, outcome tracking), event-log (immutable platform event stream), audit-log (PII access and mutation audit trail), vector-embeddings (Pinecone record references), BAI (BPFS model outputs, BLIN lender intelligence snapshots, BII industry benchmarks, BMS macro signals), marketplace (capital product catalog, deal flow records), lender (lender profiles, underwriting criteria), EDO (EDO tenant profiles, licensing terms), and telemetry (Snowflake staging tables)
  - Every schema has tenant_id column with PostgreSQL RLS policies enforcing per-tenant isolation
  - Every schema has created_at, updated_at timestamps and soft-delete pattern (deleted_at nullable) where applicable
  - Foreign key relationships documented between schemas with explicit cascade and restrict policies
  - Service ownership declared for each schema: which service has write access, which services have read-only access
  - Index strategy documented per schema: primary key indexes, tenant_id composite indexes, high-cardinality lookup indexes
  - All PII-containing columns tagged in DDL comments per §4.4 field classification standard (#1653)
  - Schemas 13-35 DDL passes forward and rollback migration tests per §14.1 (#1697)
---

## Details

Engineering spec §4.2 covers the full DDL for all 35 proprietary data schemas that form the BANKABLE IQ data moat described in Blueprint §33. Issue #1625 covered schemas 1-12 (identity, org, readiness, compliance, vault, credit, coaching, pathway, billing, notification, partner, application). Issue #1650 covered two specific tables (identity.users and readiness.snapshots). This issue covers the remaining schemas 13-35 that are referenced throughout the spec but not yet tracked as implementation work.

The 35-schema architecture is the defensive moat described in Blueprint §33 and §34: the compounding data strategy where each platform interaction adds signal to the proprietary dataset that eventually enables the BPFS predictive model to outperform any competitor without that dataset.

Key decisions:
- Schema count: Blueprint v1.8 specifies 35 schemas (25 readiness + 5 credit + 5 BAI-powered). The DDL must account for all 35.
- Event log schema is append-only (no updates, no deletes) - enforced at the application layer with RLS that blocks UPDATE and DELETE
- Audit log requires field-level encryption for any PII per §4.4 (#1653)
- Telemetry schemas are Snowflake staging tables, not PostgreSQL — they receive data from the Kafka/EventBridge event bus via a Snowflake Kafka connector or Fivetran feed

Must align with §4.1 Schemas 1-12 (#1625), §4.4 Data Lifecycle (#1653), §4.3 Data Warehouse (#1674), §8.4 Message Queue (#1693), Blueprint §33 Data Moat Architecture (#1640), and §34 35 Data Schemas.

References: engineering-spec-v1.0.html §4.2 35 Schemas Full DDL

items.title: Support interactive notebook-user auth for the `fabric` destination (Fabric Warehouse + OneLake staging)

labels.name: needs maintainer
labels.description: Potentially serious; needs proactive maintainer attention.

items.body:
### Feature description

Make the `fabric` destination usable from inside a Microsoft Fabric Python notebook under an interactive user identity — i.e. the case where `notebookutils.credentials.getToken(...)` is the canonical way to obtain AAD tokens for both the Fabric Warehouse TDS endpoint and OneLake staging, and no Service Principal is (or should be) available.

Today, `dlt[fabric]==1.24.0` hardcodes Service Principal authentication on both the warehouse side and the staging side, plus two unrelated trailing-slash defects in `FilesystemClient` cause OneLake-backed staging to return `403 ClientAuthenticationError` (instead of `404 ResourceNotFoundError`) during `initialize_storage`. Together these make the destination unreachable from a notebook without either a proper Service Principal or a non-trivial pile of runtime monkey patches.

I have a working end-to-end fix validated against a live Fabric tenant with a two-run `scd2` smoke test, and I'm opening one PR to land it.

### Are you a dlt user?

Yes, I use dlt in a Microsoft Fabric Python notebook to load data into a Fabric Warehouse with OneLake-backed staging.

### Use case

Running `dlt.pipeline(destination="fabric", staging="filesystem").run(...)` from inside a Fabric notebook is the natural entry point for many Fabric users — notebooks are how Fabric exposes interactive Python development, and they come with a blessed auth path via `notebookutils.credentials.getToken(...)`. A Fabric user already has a workspace identity and Warehouse/Lakehouse grants tied to that identity; asking them to additionally provision a Service Principal, grant it roles, and store its secret just to use dlt is a high bar that they will normally not clear.

The blocking failure chain I hit in this environment, in the order each problem fires during a single `pipeline.run(...)`:

1. **`FabricCredentials.get_odbc_dsn_dict`** (`dlt/destinations/impl/fabric/configuration.py:55-72`) unconditionally emits `AUTHENTICATION=ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal` and reads `UID`/`PWD` from `azure_client_id`/`azure_client_secret`. There is no code path for passing a pre-fetched AAD bearer token to `pyodbc` via `SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN (1256)`. The `on_partial` fallback to `DefaultAzureCredential` is also unusable in this environment — Microsoft Learn explicitly states that `DefaultAzureCredential` is not supported inside Fabric notebooks, and nothing plumbs a `TokenCredential` token into `pyodbc.connect` anyway because `FabricSqlClient` inherits `PyOdbcMsSqlClient.open_connection`, which calls `pyodbc.connect(dsn, timeout=...)` with no `attrs_before` hook.

2. **`FabricCopyFileLoadJob._ensure_fabric_token_initialized`** (`dlt/destinations/impl/fabric/fabric.py:62-139`) is triggered whenever `staging_credentials` is an `AzureServicePrincipalCredentialsWithoutDefaults` instance — which the config resolver picks any time the `azure_*` fields are populated, even with dummy strings. The helper builds a real `ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)` from those fields and hits `https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/.default` before every load, failing with `ClientAuthenticationError: 'Forbidden'` long before any data moves. The helper's own comment documents that it is a Fabric SP rate-limiting workaround, which is not needed under interactive user identity — the subsequent `COPY INTO` for OneLake does not emit a `CREDENTIAL` clause and relies on the Fabric Warehouse's workspace identity.

3. **OneLake staging ignores Fabric's built-in credential provider when any credential is supplied** (`dlt/common/configuration/specs/azure_credentials.py:118-125, 162-187` + `dlt/common/storages/fsspec_filesystem.py:95, 191`). Fabric notebooks ship a custom `OnelakeFileSystem` (in `fsspec_wrapper.trident.core`) that is registered as the `abfss://` protocol handler. Its `__init__` calls a built-in `make_credential()` helper when no `credential` kwarg is supplied, producing a `PandasCredential` tied to the notebook user identity. This is the supported OneLake auth path for interactive execution. dlt's default `AzureServicePrincipalCredentials.to_adlfs_credentials` returns SP kwargs that authenticate as a broken SP in this case; passing an explicit `TokenCredential` via `credential=` works in direct adlfs preflight calls but still returns `403` inside dlt's full load path. The only shape that works end-to-end is to omit `credential` entirely and let `OnelakeFileSystem.make_credential()` run.

4. **`FilesystemClient.dataset_path` trailing slash** (`dlt/destinations/impl/filesystem/filesystem.py:587-591`) forces the result to end in `/` via `self.pathlib.join(self.bucket_path, self.dataset_name, "")`. `FilesystemClient.initialize_storage` then calls `self.fs_client.isdir(self.dataset_path)`, which reaches `adlfs._exists` → `BlobClient.exists(version_id=...)` for a blob name ending in `/`. OneLake returns `403 ClientAuthenticationError` for the invalid shape (other Azure Blob endpoints return `404`), and the load fails at `step=load`. Reproduction, same fs instance and same path minus one character: `fs.isdir("<ws>/<lh>/Files/_dlt_stage/demo/")` → `403`, `fs.isdir("<ws>/<lh>/Files/_dlt_stage/demo")` → `True`.

5. **`FilesystemClient.get_table_dir` trailing slash** (`dlt/destinations/impl/filesystem/filesystem.py:874-883`) has the same bug one level deeper: `table_dir = self.pathlib.dirname(table_prefix) + self.pathlib.sep`. `FilesystemClient.truncate_tables` (line 721) iterates these paths and calls `self.fs_client.exists(table_dir)`, hitting the same 403 on every table once `dataset_path` is fixed.

Problems (4) and (5) are latent defects in `FilesystemClient` triggerable outside the Fabric case on any backend where `BlobClient.exists` distinguishes `foo/` from `foo` on the existence path — Fabric/OneLake just makes them visibly fatal because it responds `403` instead of `404`.

### Proposed solution

One PR that addresses all five problems together:

1. **Fabric warehouse token auth.** Add `access_token: Optional[TSecretStrValue]` to `FabricCredentials`. When set, `get_odbc_dsn_dict` returns only `DRIVER`/`SERVER`/`DATABASE`/`Encrypt`/`TrustServerCertificate`/`LongAsMax` (no `AUTHENTICATION`/`UID`/`PWD`), and `FabricSqlClient.open_connection` is overridden to pack the token into the little-endian UTF-16 struct the ODBC driver expects and pass it via `pyodbc.connect(dsn, attrs_before={1256: token_struct}, timeout=...)`. Inherited datetimeoffset output converter and autocommit behavior are preserved. SP path is untouched when no `access_token` is set.

2. **Gate the Fabric SP session warmup.** Change `FabricCopyFileLoadJob._ensure_fabric_token_initialized` to short-circuit when the credentials object lacks a real SP secret (e.g. `credentials.azure_client_secret` is `None` / empty, or the token-auth mode from (1) is active). Interactive identity loads skip the warmup and rely on the workspace identity for OneLake reads, the way `COPY INTO` already expects.

3. **Notebook-identity OneLake staging.** Teach `AzureCredentialsWithoutDefaults.to_adlfs_credentials` and `AzureServicePrincipalCredentialsWithoutDefaults.to_adlfs_credentials` to return only `{account_name, account_host}` (no `credential`, no SP fields) when the configuration is in notebook-identity mode and the bucket host is a `*.fabric.microsoft.com` endpoint. With no `credential` kwarg, the Fabric-registered `OnelakeFileSystem.__init__` falls through to its `make_credential()` helper and uses the notebook user identity for every OneLake request.

4. **Strip trailing slash from `FilesystemClient.dataset_path`.** Change the property to `self.pathlib.join(self.bucket_path, self.dataset_name)`. All other consumers use `pathlib.join(dataset_path, ...)` to append further segments, where a trailing slash is irrelevant.

5. **Strip trailing slash from `FilesystemClient.get_table_dir`.** Change `table_dir = self.pathlib.dirname(table_prefix) + self.pathlib.sep` to `table_dir = self.pathlib.dirname(table_prefix)`. Same reasoning as (4).

Validation accompanying the PR:

- 30 mocked pytest cases exercising every patched seam under fake `pyodbc`/`notebookutils`/`jwt`/adlfs — covering the struct layout for `SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, the DSN fields, the `to_adlfs_credentials` output for all four azure credentials classes in the hierarchy (both with- and without-defaults variants), the `dataset_path`/`get_table_dir` shapes, and the warmup no-op.
- Full end-to-end run against a live Fabric tenant: `dlt.pipeline(destination="fabric", staging="filesystem")` with `merge`/`scd2` disposition, two sequential runs, verification query returns the expected three-row history (`id=1` unchanged active, `id=2` original version closed at `t2`, new active version from `t2`).
- Validated against `devel` at commit `fa1e403ef3368fca80354085e55e86e11b514e8e`.

### Related issues

None found in a search of the `dlt-hub/dlt` tracker for "Fabric notebook", "OneLake 403", "`SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN`", or "`dataset_path` trailing". Happy to cross-link anything maintainers point at.

items.title: [BUG] conditions_timeline view never builds: ConditionsTimelineView selects outdated gold/transactions column names

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: Possible defect or something isn't working as documented or expected

items.body:
## Summary

The `conditions_timeline` view has never been built successfully. `ConditionsTimelineView.py` selects columns from `gold/transactions` using an outdated schema (`end_to_end_id`, `tenant_id`, `tx_type`, `tx_msg_id`, `tx_status`, `tx_amount`, `tx_ccy`), but the gold transactions table written by `TransactionsETL.py` has `endtoendid`, `tenantid`, `txtp`, `msgid`, `txsts`, `amt`, `ccy`. Spark fails column resolution on every run and the ViewsOrchestrator swallows the error, so `views/conditions_timeline` never materializes.

## Evidence (AWS beta deployment, Server C, 2026-09-08)

Every pipeline cycle logs:

```
[ConditionsTimelineViewETL] Creating Conditions Timeline View...
[ViewsOrchestrator] Skipping conditions_timeline due to error: [UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION] A column or function parameter with name `t`.`end_to_end_id` cannot be resolved. Did you mean one of the following? [`t`.`endtoendid`, `t`.`event_date`, `t`.`event_ts`, `t`.`tenantid`, `t`.`event_to_ingest_ms`].;
```

...followed by `FULL PIPELINE COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!`, so nothing surfaces the failure.

Live Hudi commit schema of `gold/transactions`:

```
transaction_id, amt, ccy, credttm, destination, endtoendid, msgid, source, tenantid, txsts, txtp, event_ts, event_date, created_at_epoch_ms, ingested_at_ts, event_to_ingest_ms, source_file_path, record_hash
```

The datalakehouse-api logs `WARNING:pipeline:Path for table 'conditions_timeline' not found: /opt/Tazama_Warehouse/views/conditions_timeline` on every query and returns empty result sets with HTTP 200.

## Impact

The CMS backend (`case-management-system/backend/src/modules/gold-lakehouse/condition-lakehouse.service.ts`) queries `FROM conditions_timeline` for the condition timeline visualizations (`cond_account_id` endpoints in `gold-lakehouse.controller.ts`). These render permanently empty. No error is raised anywhere in the chain (orchestrator prints-and-skips, API returns 200 with empty rows, CMS renders blank), which is why this went unnoticed.

## Root cause

Commit `44f45db` (2026-07-10) changed the transactions table source to event_history and renamed its columns to the raw names (`endtoendid`, `tenantid`, `txtp`, ...). `ConditionsTimelineView.py` (`_load_transactions`) was not updated and still selects the old snake_case names. Only the transactions select is affected - `gold/condition`, `gold/alerts`, `gold/cases`, `gold/tasks` column references in the view all match their live schemas.

## Scope of fix

In `_load_transactions`, remap the eight columns and alias them back to the existing internal names so the view's output schema (consumed by the CMS) is unchanged:

```python
t = t0.select(
    F.col("t.transaction_id"),
    F.col("t.endtoendid").alias("end_to_end_id"),
    F.col("t.tenantid").alias("tx_tenant_id"),
    F.col("t.txtp").alias("tx_type"),
    F.col("t.msgid").alias("tx_msg_id"),
    F.col("t.txsts").alias("tx_status"),
    F.col("t.amt").alias("tx_amount"),
    F.col("t.ccy").alias("tx_ccy"),
    F.col("t.event_ts").alias("tx_event_ts"),
    F.col("t.event_date").alias("tx_event_date"),
)
```

Note: `_load_transactions` currently aliases `tenant_id` to `tx_tenant_id` inside the select, so downstream join/select logic keeps working with the aliases above; no other changes required.

## Secondary observation

The bug class is enabled by the ViewsOrchestrator catching all exceptions per view and reporting overall success. Consider failing the run (or at least a non-success status) when a view build errors, so schema drift like this is caught immediately.

items.title: Report data exports

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

Several stories in this epic assume an export exists — #384 exports indicator aggregates, #385 exports receivables, #591 bundles an assessment pack, #593 attaches artefacts to scheduled deliveries — but no export capability has been built. Each of those would otherwise implement its own CSV writer, its own file naming, its own delivery mechanism and its own audit record, which guarantees inconsistency in exactly the area where inconsistency is most expensive.

Export is the point at which data leaves the platform's control. Once a file is downloaded, RLS, OpenFGA, the audit trail and the platform's retention schedule have all ended; the hospital, as Data Fiduciary under DPDP 2023, remains accountable for personal data it can no longer see, restrict or erase. The platform's own audit rules list data exports alongside prescriptions, refunds and break-glass access as events requiring tamper-evident records, and the tenant isolation rules call out data-export controls explicitly. An export capability built casually undermines every access control built carefully elsewhere.

There is an operational dimension too. Hospital finance and MIS staff genuinely need data in Excel — for board packs, for auditor submissions, for the accountant's own reconciliation — and refusing exports simply pushes them to screenshots, copy-paste and unmanaged database access, which is strictly worse. And exports are frequently large: a year of invoice lines or encounter facts is not a synchronous HTTP response, so a naive implementation will time out on the first real request and produce a truncated file that the recipient will not notice is truncated.

Affected roles: finance controller, MIS clerk, quality manager, hospital administrator, TPA co-ordinator, laboratory and pharmacy managers, the DPO and the platform security team.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** finance controller
**I want** to export any report I am entitled to as a complete, correctly formatted file delivered by a time-limited link
**So that** I can work with the data outside the platform, while the hospital retains a full record of what was exported, by whom and containing what.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A shared export service consumed by every report in this epic, so no report implements its own file writing or delivery.
* Formats: CSV (RFC 4180), XLSX with typed columns and frozen headers, PDF for presentation reports and compliance packs, and JSON for machine consumption.
* Asynchronous job model with progress, cancellation and streaming generation so file size is bounded by storage, not by request timeout.
* Delivery exclusively by signed, time-limited object-storage URLs scoped to the requesting user; never a direct download from an application response, never a permanent URL.
* Export manifest per job recording the report, parameters, resolved period, row count, column list, sensitivity classification, requester and generation time, embedded in the file where the format permits and always stored server-side.
* Entitlement enforcement at generation time using the same field-level relations as #592, with a distinct exporter relation separate from viewing.
* Per-tenant and per-user export quotas, row caps by sensitivity class, and an approval step for exports above a configured row threshold or containing identifying fields.
* Tamper-evident audit record per export, and a tenant-visible export register the DPO can review.
* Retention: generated artefacts expire and are deleted from object storage after a configurable period, default 7 days.

**Out of scope**

* Report content, query logic and the semantic layer — owned by #583–#592.
* Scheduling and channel delivery of exports — owned by #593, which calls this service.
* Bulk data extraction for migration, warehousing or ETL to a customer's own systems — that is a platform data-portability concern, not report export.
* DPDP data-principal access requests producing a patient's own record copy — that is the rights workflow in the Security and Compliance epic, which has different content and identity-verification requirements.
* Direct database or warehouse credentials issued to tenants.

---

## Recommended Solution

Build `export-service` as a Go module invoked over an internal interface by report handlers, never called directly by the browser with a report payload. The caller passes a report reference and parameters; the service re-executes the query itself. This matters: if the client supplied the rows, the export would inherit whatever the client had rather than what the requester is entitled to, and the manifest could not be trusted.

**Job model and data:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE export_job (
  job_id         uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id      uuid NOT NULL,
  facility_id    uuid,
  requested_by   uuid NOT NULL,
  source_kind    text NOT NULL CHECK (source_kind IN ('fixed_report','custom_definition','pack')),
  source_key     text NOT NULL,
  parameters     jsonb NOT NULL,
  format         text NOT NULL CHECK (format IN ('csv','xlsx','pdf','json')),
  sensitivity    text NOT NULL CHECK (sensitivity IN
                   ('aggregate','financial','clinical','identifying')),
  status         text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN
                   ('queued','awaiting_approval','running','completed','failed',
                    'cancelled','expired','denied')),
  row_count      int,
  byte_size      bigint,
  object_key     text,
  checksum_sha256 text,
  approved_by    uuid,
  requested_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  completed_at   timestamptz,
  expires_at     timestamptz,
  idempotency_key text,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, requested_by, idempotency_key),
  CONSTRAINT approval_required CHECK (
    sensitivity <> 'identifying' OR status IN ('queued','awaiting_approval','denied','cancelled')
      OR approved_by IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE export_manifest_column (
  job_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES export_job ON DELETE CASCADE,
  ordinal int NOT NULL, field_key text NOT NULL,
  display_name text NOT NULL, sensitivity text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (job_id, ordinal)
);
```

The `approval_required` check enforces in the database what policy states: an export containing identifying fields cannot reach `completed` without a recorded approver. Putting this in a constraint rather than only in service code means no future code path can bypass it.

**Generation** runs as a Temporal workflow: authorise → estimate rows → gate on quota, cap and approval → stream-generate → checksum → store → sign → notify. Generation streams from a server-side cursor over the analytics cluster directly into an object-storage multipart upload, so peak memory is a buffer rather than a result set, and a 2-million-row CSV is bounded by time and storage rather than by heap. XLSX uses a streaming writer for the same reason; PDF is generated section-wise with checkpointing, matching the pack approach in #591. The SHA-256 checksum is recorded and shown to the requester so a truncated or corrupted download is detectable — a silently truncated financial export is the failure mode that does real damage, because nobody notices a file that opens successfully.

**Delivery.** The only egress is a signed object-storage URL with a short expiry, default 15 minutes, bound to the requesting user and single-use where the storage provider supports it. Artefacts are stored under tenant-dedicated storage paths, and object lifecycle rules delete them at `expires_at` regardless of application state, so retention does not depend on a cleanup job running.

**API surface:**

* `POST /api/v1/exports` — body carries source reference, parameters, format; returns job id. `Idempotency-Key` header required.
* `GET /api/v1/exports/{job_id}` — status, progress, row count, checksum.
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/download-url` — mints a fresh signed URL; each mint is separately audited.
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/cancel`
* `POST /api/v1/exports/{job_id}/approve` — requires the approver relation, records the approver.
* `GET /api/v1/exports/register?from=&to=&user_id=` — the tenant export register for the DPO.

**Events published:** `ExportRequested`, `ExportApproved`, `ExportCompleted`, `ExportDownloaded`, `ExportDenied`, `ExportExpired`. `ExportDownloaded` is emitted on each signed-URL mint, not on job completion, because the auditable act is retrieval, not generation.

**OpenFGA:**

```
type export_job
  relations
    define facility: [facility]
    define requester: [user]
    define exporter_aggregate: quality_manager from facility or hospital_admin from facility
    define exporter_financial: finance_controller from facility
    define exporter_identifying: hospital_admin from facility
    define approver: dpo from tenant or hospital_admin from facility
    define register_viewer: dpo from tenant
```

Export relations are deliberately narrower than the corresponding view relations across this epic — being able to read a receivables report on screen is not the same permission as taking it out of the platform. The approver is a different person from the requester by construction: the service rejects self-approval even where a user holds both relations.

**Sequencing.** Must land alongside or before #593, which attaches exports to scheduled deliveries, and it consumes the field sensitivity classifications defined by #592's semantic layer. Fixed-report exports for #384 and #385 can be wired first while the semantic layer is still in progress.

**Risks.** The largest is an export whose contents no longer match its entitlements because the query re-ran after a permission change mid-job — mitigated by resolving relations once at job start, recording them on the job, and failing the job rather than downgrading if a relation is revoked during generation. Quota exhaustion by one tenant degrading generation for others is contained by a per-tenant worker concurrency limit. Signed URLs being forwarded is mitigated by short expiry, user binding and single-use where supported, and accepted as residual risk otherwise — which is precisely why identifying exports require approval and appear in the DPO's register.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a finance controller holding `exporter_financial` for her facility requests an XLSX export of the last quarter's receivables ageing report
**When** the export job runs to completion
**Then** the file contains every row the on-screen report would show for the same parameters with typed columns and a frozen header, the manifest records the report, resolved period, row count, column list and requester, the download is delivered by a signed URL expiring in 15 minutes, the recorded SHA-256 matches the downloaded file, and `ExportCompleted` followed by `ExportDownloaded` appear in the tamper-evident audit trail.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a user requests an export containing patient-identifying columns and holds `exporter_identifying` but there is no separate approver
**When** the job is created
**Then** it is held at `awaiting_approval`, no file is generated and no URL is minted, an approval request is raised to the DPO, self-approval by the requester is rejected even though they hold the approver relation, and if approval is refused the job moves to `denied` with the refusal recorded in the export register.

### Edge Cases

* Generation fails at 80% of a 2-million-row CSV — no partial object is exposed, the multipart upload is aborted, the job moves to `failed` with the stage recorded, and the requester is told to retry rather than being handed a truncated file.
* The same request is submitted twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` — the second returns the existing job rather than generating a duplicate file and a second audit entry.
* A requester's exporter relation is revoked while the job is running — the job fails closed with `denied`, and no URL is minted for an already-generated object.
* A signed URL is requested after `expires_at` — minting is refused, the object is already deleted by the storage lifecycle rule, and the requester is directed to raise a fresh job rather than the artefact being silently regenerated.
* An export resolves to zero rows — a file is still produced containing headers and the manifest, so the recipient can distinguish an empty result from a failed generation.
* A field containing a leading `=`, `+` or `-` is written to CSV — it is neutralised so the file cannot execute a formula on open in a spreadsheet, a genuine injection path in exported reports.
* A tenant exceeds its monthly export quota — further requests are refused with the quota and reset date named, existing running jobs complete, and other tenants are unaffected.

---
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** any entitled user exports any report they can view, in a format fit for the tool they will use it in, delivered by a short-lived link with a verifiable checksum and a complete manifest.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** screenshots, copy-paste and unmanaged database access are displaced by a single governed egress path, and the DPO can answer what left the platform, when, to whom and containing what, from one register.
* **Success metric or validation method:** a 2-million-row CSV generates within 5 minutes with steady-state memory under 256 MB per worker; 100% of completed exports carry a manifest, checksum and audit record, asserted by an invariant test over the job table; zero exports completed with identifying sensitivity and no distinct approver, enforced by the database constraint and verified adversarially; zero cross-tenant object access across the isolation test suite; artefact deletion at `expires_at` verified by an object-storage lifecycle audit.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 8 weeks post-deployment, tracking job outcome distribution, p95 generation time by format and row band, quota refusal rate, approval turnaround for identifying exports, and orphaned-object count in tenant storage paths (target zero).

---
## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — "The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level" and "Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly", as applied to the generated artefacts themselves.
**Reason:** the export service's own UI surface is small — a format chooser, a job progress state and a download control — and those are covered in full. The exported CSV, XLSX and PDF files are consumed in third-party applications whose accessibility the platform cannot control, and a WCAG conformance claim cannot meaningfully be made about a spreadsheet.
**Alternative validation:** the in-platform export controls, progress states, approval flow and export register are tested to the agreed WCAG level with keyboard operation and screen-reader labelling; generated PDFs are produced with a document title, logical reading order and tagged headings so they are not gratuitously inaccessible; XLSX carries proper column headers and typed cells rather than a single text column.
**Residual risk:** a recipient using assistive technology may encounter a poorly navigable file in their spreadsheet application. Low impact, as the same data remains available in the accessible on-screen report.
**Approved by:** Design System lead and Head of Data, to be recorded on the pull request.

items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |
| Row-Level Security | 讓資料庫本身強制每列資料能被哪個租戶看到。 | 由資料庫在每一列層級強制租戶存取政策。 | PostgreSQL RLS、session context、policy。 | 交易開始設定tenant context，並測試直接SQL與服務帳號路徑。 | 共享schema的強制隔離。 | 繞過RLS的管理連線很危險；政策需納入migration與測試。 |
| Tenant-aware API | API 從驗證到查詢都必須知道目前是哪個租戶。 | API在授權、資料查詢與回應中都理解租戶邊界。 | JWT、middleware、OPA、quota。 | middleware解析tenant，服務層拒絕不一致context並套用配額。 | 多租戶REST/GraphQL服務。 | 不要只在controller過濾；內部服務與webhook也要驗證。 |
| Multi-tenant Scaling | 避免單一大租戶吃光資源，並能依租戶分片、限流與擴容。 | 在租戶數、流量與資料量成長時維持隔離與效能。 | Quota、sharding、partition、autoscaling、noisy-neighbor control。 | 依租戶分片/限流，監控單租戶資源與升級路徑。 | SaaS成長與大型租戶加入。 | 平均容量會掩蓋熱租戶；需壓測最壞分布。 |

## AI 系統從建置到上線：三段流程

閱讀順序只有三段：**先準備資料 → 再處理使用者請求 → 最後用線上結果持續改善**。底部三項是每個階段都必須具備的系統能力。

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph PREP["A. 事前準備：把資料變成 AI 可用的知識"]
    direction LR
    DE["1. Data Engineering<br/>收集、清理、治理資料"]
    DS["2. Data Science<br/>分析資料、定義指標與特徵"]
    ML["3. ML 基礎<br/>選模型、Embedding 與推論方式"]
    KB[("可檢索知識庫<br/>Chunks + Metadata + Vectors")]
    DE --> DS --> ML --> KB
  end

  subgraph REQUEST["B. 線上請求：使用者問問題時，系統實際怎麼跑"]
    direction LR
    USER["使用者 / 前端"] --> API["API 接收問題"]
    API --> RAG["4. RAG / LLM Application<br/>找資料、排序、組 Prompt"]
    RAG --> NEED{"需要執行動作？"}
    NEED -->|否| ANSWER["LLM 產生答案"]
    NEED -->|是| AGENT["5. Agent<br/>規劃步驟、呼叫工具、保存狀態"]
    AGENT --> ANSWER
    ANSWER --> USER
  end

  KB -->|提供相關資料| RAG

  subgraph IMPROVE["C. 上線後：觀察結果並持續改善"]
    direction LR
    OBS["6. Production AI / Observability<br/>記錄品質、延遲、成本與錯誤"]
    EVAL["7. LLM Evaluation<br/>Golden Dataset、Judge、Faithfulness"]
    FIX["修正資料 / Prompt / 模型 / 流程"]
    OBS --> EVAL --> FIX
  end

  ANSWER -->|留下 Trace 與 Feedback| OBS
  FIX -->|重新發佈| RAG
  FIX -->|補資料與品質規則| DE

  CROSS["所有階段共同要求<br/>8. Multi-tenant：租戶與資料隔離<br/>9. AI Security / Reliability：權限、PII、Guardrails<br/>10. Architecture：Queue、Cache、Scaling、Fault Tolerance"]
```

items.title: [SPEC] Blueprint §XIV Compounding Moat and Endgame: EDO B2B licensing API, lender plug-in subscription infrastructure, telemetry monetization layer, and vocabulary ownership tracking toward unicorn-scale valuation trajectory
items.body:
---
owner: service:platform
depends_on: ["1634", "1674"]
blocks: []
spec_sections: ["§5.5"]
blueprint_sections: ["§XIV", "§33"]
maturity_target: Compounding Capital
acceptance:
  - EDO (Economic Development Organization) licensing API implemented: POST /edo/tenant/provision, GET /edo/tenant/:id/config, PATCH /edo/tenant/:id/branding — allows SBDCs, CDFIs, chambers, franchise systems, and accelerators to spin up white-labeled BANKABLE IQ instances
  - EDO tenant provisioning automated: EDO signs up via Enterprise tier, Stripe billing activates, PostgreSQL tenant is provisioned with EDO-specific branding config, and EDO admin account is created — all within 60 seconds, no manual HQ intervention
  - Lender plug-in subscription infrastructure implemented: lenders pay a B2B subscription to access the Capital Marketplace API per §5.7 (#1634), receive a dedicated API key scoped to their subscription tier, and are billed via Stripe B2B invoicing
  - Telemetry monetization layer designed: Snowflake data schema (#1674) captures anonymized cross-tenant signals that form the proprietary intelligence dataset; data governance policy implemented to ensure no PII or tenant-identifiable data in the monetization layer
  - Vocabulary ownership tracker implemented as an internal tool: tracks how often the term Bankability Score, Bankability Compass, and Bankable Standard appear in external content (news, government documents, industry reports) as an early signal of category ownership per Blueprint §01
  - B2B API pricing tiers documented and implemented in Stripe: EDO Basic (public-facing Compass + intake), EDO Professional (full Wheel + coaching), EDO Enterprise (full platform white-label)
  - EDO usage reporting implemented: monthly usage summary per EDO tenant with assessment counts, score distributions, module completions, and capital pathway activations for HQ business intelligence
---

## Details

Blueprint §XIV covers the Compounding Moat and Endgame — the long-term strategic infrastructure that transforms BANKABLE from a SaaS product into a category-defining institution. The two primary components are the EDO (Economic Development Organization) licensing model (B2B distribution) and the lender plug-in subscription marketplace (B2B revenue from institutional capital providers).

These are explicitly the infrastructure required to achieve the unicorn-scale valuation trajectory described in Blueprint §XIV ($25M → $10B+). The EDO licensing model allows BANKABLE to distribute through existing trusted channels (SBDCs, CDFIs, chambers) without building a direct sales force. The lender plug-in model inverts the traditional capital marketplace by making lenders pay to access Bankable-qualified deal flow.

Key decisions:
- EDO isolation model: EDO tenants are fully isolated (dedicated PostgreSQL schemas with RLS) or logically isolated (same schema with EDO-specific tenant_id prefix)? Blueprint §XII Layer 11 Infrastructure Layer implies full isolation
- Data sovereignty for EDO licensees: EDO clients' assessment data — does it flow into the central Bankable telemetry moat or stay within the EDO tenant boundary?
- Vocabulary tracking is a lightweight intelligence function, not a platform feature for clients — it feeds HQ competitive intelligence, not any client-facing surface

Must align with Blueprint §33 Data Moat (#1640), §5.7 Capital Marketplace API (#1634), §4.3 Data Warehouse (#1674), §10.2 RBAC Roles (#1682), §17.1 Infrastructure Cost Model (#1684), and Blueprint §XII 12-Layer Architecture.

References: Blueprint v1.8 §XIV The Compounding Moat and Endgame

items.title: [P1-1·库存] 盘点单「出任务」仓库下拉为空：开租不种默认仓 + 无任何建仓入口

labels.name: needs-verification
labels.description: 需要 AI 自动验收的 issue

items.body:
## 现象（2026-10-24 用户实测，截图逐字）

盘点单页 →「出盘点任务」→「仓库」下拉**只有占位项**，无法出任务。用户原话：
「盘点单的上的仓库下拉选择没有数据，这个需要在先创建仓库吧？在哪去创建？」

## 根因链（读码，非推断）

1. `warehouses` 表在该环境下 **0 行**：`WarehouseService.defaultWarehouse()` 注释逐字「段 1 不自动建，缺省由调用方明说」；`docs/deployment/demo-seed.sql` 也没有任何 warehouses 插入。
2. **前端没有建仓入口**：admin-web 的 `warehouseApi` 只有只读 `list()`；菜单「仓储与物料」= 库存明细/盘点单/发货单/余料台账/省料看板，「供应链」= 入库单/供应商/采购单 —— 没有「仓库」节点。盘点页注释自陈「不在本页建仓 / 改仓（仓库主数据归仓储域；本页只**选**仓）」，而那个「仓储域」页面至今未落地。
3. 后端接口存在但无人调用：`POST /api/admin/warehouses`（码 `inbound:create`）。管理员密码登录已禁用（#375），所以「手工 curl 建仓」也不构成可用出路。
4. 附带：即便建了仓，`StocktakeService.open` 只快照 `stock_batches.warehouse = warehouses.code`（**文本相等**）且 `quantity > 0` 的批次；而入库单的「仓库 / 仓位」是**自由文本**（`InboundOrderService` 逐字 `trimToNull(req.getWarehouse())`）⇒ 文本不与 code 对齐时盘点单是 **0 行明细**。

## 修法（用户 2026-10-24 裁定：零 UI 最小解）

1. **开租即种默认主仓**：新增 `WarehouseSeedService.seedDefaultWarehouse(tenantId)`（幂等），在 `RegistrationService.seedRequiredInitialData` 里接线，并登记进 `OnboardingInitialData.REQUIRED`（enforced）+ 入驻后置条件校验 —— 缺仓 ⇒ 开租 fail-closed（沿用 #6295/#7148 的类级固化形态）。
2. **存量租户回填**：V189 迁移给「一个仓都没有」的租户补一条默认主仓（幂等 `NOT EXISTS`）。
3. **出任务时「未指定仓」归默认仓**：默认仓除了 `warehouse = code`，也收 `warehouse` 为空/空白的批次（旧数据 + 入库单留空），并收「写成仓名」的批次 —— **不改写任何历史文本**。

## 判据（会红）

- 真库：空库真跑入驻链路 ⇒ 该租户 `warehouses` 恰 **1** 行、`code`/`name` = 单一来源常量、`is_default = true`、`tenant_id` = 新租户；再调一次播种 ⇒ 0 行（幂等）。
- 红证 A：摘掉仓种子 + 摘掉后置条件探针 ⇒ 入驻「成功」但仓 **0** 行（= 本单的原始形态）。
- 红证 B：只摘掉仓种子、保留后置条件 ⇒ 入驻**当场失败**（`ONBOARDING_REQUIRED_DATA_MISSING`，键含 `default_warehouse`）。
- 真库：默认仓出任务 ⇒ 快照包含 `warehouse` 为空的批次；非默认仓不包含。
- 类级元守卫：`tests/unit_ci_workflows/test_onboarding_required_seed_guard.py` 自动对账（未登记即红、后置条件键必须在断言方法体内）。

## 边界（照实登记）

- **不自动改写**历史批次上的仓库自由文本：文本既不是 code 也不是仓名、且非空的批次**不会**计入默认仓盘点（那属于「多仓建档页」的归属，后续段）。
- 不做仓库管理页 / 调拨页（用户明确选「零 UI」）—— 多仓仍只能走 `POST /api/admin/warehouses`。
- 库存滞销报表「按仓筛选」用 `warehouseCode`（= code）与批次文本比对 ⇒ 对历史自由文本不生效（本单不修，登记为后续）。
- 迁移只补「一个仓都没有」的租户，不动已有仓档案的租户（不碰 `is_default` 唯一索引）。

items.title: perf(chart-data): ensure_totals_available re-runs percent-metric totals query on every request, bypassing QueryCacheManager (INC-B1081392)

labels.name: incident-autopilot
labels.description: Created by the incident triage automation

labels.name: autopilot-managed
labels.description: Admit this issue to the Devin remediation control plane

items.body:
<!-- devin-autopilot-run:INC-B1081392 -->

**Incident:** `datadog:incident:a75a6a38-caeb-4c08-b0bf-a9a81571b545` (SEV-3, service `luma-embedded-analytics`, scenario CD-1)
**Attribution confidence:** 0.8 (agent report) — independently confirmed by code inspection at `4511c13` (see "Confirmation" below).

## Customer impact
Embedded table charts that use percent metrics with `percent_metric_calculation = 'all_records'` intermittently exceed the host app's 5 s render budget under multi-tenant load. Signals at trigger: chart timeout rate 18.7% (threshold 5%), p95 chart latency 6320 ms, 14 tenants affected. Other chart types (`big_number_total`, `echarts_timeseries_line`) on the same dashboards/tenants had 0 timeouts.

## Observed behavior
On every synchronous `POST /api/v1/chart/data` for such a table, the "totals" query (`SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM orders WHERE tenant_id=? AND order_ts ...`, no GROUP BY, full scan) is executed against the warehouse **even when the whole payload is cache-warm**. Warehouse digest: totals fingerprint ran 164× vs 21 baseline — exactly the number of 200-status chart-data requests — while the grouped query ran only 9× (served from cache). APM traces show `cache_metadata='loaded'`, `superset_status=200`, yet 6.4–7.3 s duration.

## Expected behavior
The totals query should run at most once and be served from `QueryCacheManager` (DATA region) thereafter, like the main query. A cache-warm chart-data request should issue zero warehouse queries.

## Root cause / likely code area
`QueryContextProcessor.get_payload_result()` (`superset/common/query_context_processor.py` ~L646-684) calls `ensure_totals_available()` on every non-`force_cached` request. `ensure_totals_available()` (~L605-631) does:

```python
totals_query = self._query_context.queries[totals_idx]
result = self._query_context.get_query_result(totals_query)   # <- uncached
```

`QueryContext.get_query_result` → `QueryContextProcessor.get_query_result` → `self._qc_datasource.get_query_result(query_object)` → `ExploreMixin.get_query_result()` (`superset/models/helpers.py` ~L2604) → `self.query(...)`. There is no `QueryCacheManager` lookup anywhere on this path. Afterwards the same totals query object is also processed by `get_query_results_with_timing` (cached path), so on a warm cache the totals SQL still hits the warehouse once per request.

Contrast: the async path `superset/tasks/async_queries.py::_inject_contribution_totals` (~L170-202) explicitly reads the totals dataframe from `QueryCacheManager.get(key=..., region=CacheRegion.DATA)` instead of re-running it — the intended behaviour the sync path lacks.

The extra columns-less totals query is emitted by `superset-frontend/plugins/plugin-chart-table/src/buildQuery.ts` (~L334-351) when `percent_metric_calculation === 'all_records'`; `normalize_contribution_totals()` selects it as `totals_idx`.

## Reproduction steps
1. Create a Table chart with a metric and at least one **percent metric** (e.g. `SUM(revenue)`), set *Percent metric calculation* = **All records**, and group by a dimension on a moderately large dataset.
2. Enable data caching (`DATA_CACHE_CONFIG`) and load the chart twice.
3. Observe warehouse query log / `db_engine` logs: the no-GROUP-BY `SELECT SUM(revenue) ...` query executes on **both** loads, while the grouped query executes only on the first.
4. Unit-level: build a `QueryContextProcessor` with two queries (grouped + totals with `columns=[]`), warm the DATA cache for both, mock the datasource `query`/`get_query_result`, call `get_payload_result()` → datasource is still queried once (totals). Existing tests `tests/unit_tests/common/test_query_context_processor.py::test_ensure_totals_available_updates_cache_values` show the mocking setup.

## Evidence
- RUM: all 36 timeouts are `table_v2` charts (112 views, p95 6810 ms); other viz types 0 timeouts.
- Every timed-out chart has `percent_metrics=[SUM(revenue)]` + `percent_metric_calculation='all_records'`; the one `row_limit` table is not among the timeouts.
- Warehouse: totals fingerprint 164× vs 21 baseline (p95 2140 ms, 100k rows scanned); grouped fingerprint 9× vs 12 baseline.
- Edge gateway 499s rose only on the chart-data route (client aborts on slow-but-successful responses).
- No deploys in the incident window; HEAD `4511c13` is a psycopg2-binary bump only. Latent defect from the original `all_records` feature (#33656) surfacing under load.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ensure_totals_available()` obtains the totals dataframe through the cached path (`get_df_payload_result` / `QueryCacheManager` lookup, mirroring `_inject_contribution_totals`) so the totals SQL executes at most once per cache TTL.
- [ ] A cache-warm `get_payload_result()` for an `all_records` percent-metric table issues no datasource query (new unit test in `tests/unit_tests/common/test_query_context_processor.py` asserting the datasource is not queried when the totals cache entry is loaded).
- [ ] Existing tests `test_ensure_totals_available_updates_cache_values` and `test_cache_values_sync_after_ensure_totals_available` still pass; cache keys are unaffected (`contribution_totals` remains stripped from the key).
- [ ] `force_cached=True` behaviour unchanged.

## Related-component context (not owners of the defect)
- `engineerA314/devin-demo` (embedded-analytics-product / luma-web): owns the 5000 ms render budget that converts slow 200 responses into RUM timeouts and 499s; surfaces the symptom only.
- `data-platform/warehouse-config` (analytics-warehouse): healthy; queue depth rose purely from the redundant totals query volume. Missing aggregation/indexing for the 100k-row scan is a contributing factor, and `percent_metric_calculation='row_limit'` or a higher render budget would mitigate the symptom without fixing the redundant query.

## Confirmation notes / caveats
- Confirmed by static inspection of the code path above at `4511c13`; no runtime reproduction was possible in this environment (no Python venv / pytest for the backend).
- p50 chart-data latency of ~1.36 s indicates the grouped query is itself non-trivial; the totals query is the dominant but not sole contributor.
